D009-D018_h001.question:
I work alone out on the light, so I notice every change in myself. About a year ago, after that storm when the fishing boat went down right in front of me and I could hear them on the radio and couldn’t reach them in time… things haven’t been the same since.

Since then, my sleep has been shot. I’m up most nights, replaying the waves swallowing that boat, jumping at any sound. Even when I stay up for nights in a row, I just keep pacing the station, checking the equipment over and over. I get these bursts where I can’t sit still, talking to myself out loud, almost nonstop, like if I stop talking the silence will bring those screams back. I’ll start a dozen jobs around the station at once, but it’s not really productive—more like I’m driven by nerves.

Other times, especially this past year, I just break down crying out of nowhere. I can’t get myself to do basic maintenance, and thinking through simple tasks wears me out. I’ve caught myself thinking it’d be easier if I just didn’t wake up, or if I “accidentally” went over the rail—no real plan, just that thought circling. All of this has made it hard to keep the light the way it should be.
D009-D018_h001.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Bipolar II Disorder
    C. Binge-Eating Disorder
    D. Persistent Depressive Disorder

D009-D018_h002.question:
It started after the car accident about a year ago. I thought I was fine physically, but since then I haven’t really felt like myself. Most of the time I feel…flat, like someone turned the volume down on all my emotions. I don’t get excited about projects anymore, even though I used to love planning out a space down to the smallest detail. I just stare at mood boards and can’t make myself start. I’m exhausted all the time, no matter how much I sleep, and it’s made it hard to keep up with clients and even basic house stuff.

My sleep has been awful since the crash. I’m on edge at night, jumpy at every sound, and when I do sleep I wake up wired, like my body can’t calm down. That constant jitteriness is just there now; I pace around the house or fuss with things without really doing anything useful.

There was a period a few months ago, for about a month, where I felt weirdly “up” and restless, talking nonstop to my husband, staying up most of the night reorganizing rooms and not even feeling tired. But even then, the tension and bad sleep were the same as they’ve been since the accident. Lately, when it all feels too heavy, I catch myself planning out very specifically how I might end things—where I’d do it, what I’d use. That scares me.
D009-D018_h002.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Bipolar II Disorder
    C. Binge-Eating Disorder
    D. Persistent Depressive Disorder

D009-D018_h003.question:
I’ve been a paramedic about three years. About a year and a half ago I worked a really bad call — multi‑car pileup, one of them was a kid about my sister’s age. I was with him when he died in the rig. Since then I just haven’t felt like myself.

For the past year it’s like I’m hollowed out. I go to work, but I feel numb, almost like I’m on autopilot. Stuff that used to matter — getting good performance reviews, finishing my EMT‑P cert — I just don’t care anymore. Even on my days off I’m exhausted; getting out of bed feels like dragging a body. I’ve thought a lot about ending things, down to where I’d do it and how, and I’ve caught myself planning it out.

At the same time I’m always on edge. I hardly sleep — I’ll stay up pacing or replaying scenes from calls. It’s not just a few days here and there; it’s been constant since that crash. I feel wired, restless, talk too much on shift, and I’ve been more reckless with hookups than I’m proud of. It doesn’t come in waves; it’s just there, all the time, ever since that night.
D009-D018_h003.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Bipolar II Disorder
    C. Binge-Eating Disorder
    D. Persistent Depressive Disorder

D009-D018_h004.question:
It really started about a year ago, after that lockdown drill turned into a real incident at school. We thought there was an active shooter; the kids were sobbing under their desks, and I honestly thought we were all going to die. At night I’ll be wide awake, wired, replaying that drill in my head instead of sleeping. I can go for nights with barely any sleep and still feel revved up and talk nonstop to my husband, but it doesn’t feel like a “good mood,” just this restless, anxious energy that hasn’t really let up since the incident. It’s been going on continuously, not coming and going in clear episodes, and it’s gotten to the point where it’s hard to function normally at work and at home.
D009-D018_h004.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Bipolar II Disorder
    C. Binge-Eating Disorder
    D. Persistent Depressive Disorder

D009-D018_h005.question:

I’ve also been more talkative and busy at work and with colleagues, but it doesn’t feel like a separate “up” phase; it’s been this steady, jittery overdrive ever since that case.
D009-D018_h005.options:
A. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    B. Bipolar II Disorder
    C. Binge-Eating Disorder
    D. Persistent Depressive Disorder

D009-D018_h006.question:

D009-D018_h006.options:

    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Inattentive Presentation)

D009-D018_h007.question:
I’ve been driving the subway for over twenty years, mostly nights. About a year ago, I had a man jump in front of my train. I saw his face, hit the brakes, but it was too late. Since then, it’s like my whole system’s been stuck on high alert and then completely shut down.

Sleep is awful. For the last couple of months especially, I’ve been numb during the day, going through the motions, and then at night I get these vivid, horrible dreams of the accident. I wake up drenched in sweat and can’t get back to sleep. It’s starting to affect my driving and my marriage.
D009-D018_h007.options:
A. Bipolar II Disorder
    B. Posttraumatic Stress Disorder
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Inattentive Presentation)

D009-D018_h008.question:

D009-D018_h008.options:

    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Inattentive Presentation)

D009-D018_h009.question:
